extracted.intended_audience: prospective DINFOS students, military public affairs personnel, and general readers interested in military public affairs/journalism training
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the Defense Information School's courses, learning objectives, accreditation, certification requirements, and eligibility/ progression rules for military public affairs, journalism, broadcast, photojournalism, and equipment-maintenance training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated Press (AP) Style compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are taught the fundamentals of news, journalism, and how to write and copy-edit in accordance with the Associated Press (AP) Styleguide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an explicit expectation in the Public Affairs Qualification Course (PAQC): writing and copy-editing should follow AP Style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Affairs fundamentals and military-media relations
rubrics_metrics.description: PAQC provides those who are new to the public affairs field the fundamentals of public affairs to include military-media relations, the different mediums used to facilitate the flow of accurate and timely information, and how to conduct public affairs operations in support of the command's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAQC is positioned as the foundational course for newcomers; mastery of these fundamentals is the core learning objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expeditionary PA course prerequisites and field-application focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Affairs Expeditionary Course is a ten-day, intensive follow-on course to PAQC. Students are expected to have a basic working knowledge and experience in PA as the course is focused more on the application of PA skills in a field environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation that entrants already possess basic PA knowledge/experience; emphasis on practical, field-oriented application rather than introductory theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism writing styles and headline-ese
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism classes feature basic writing skills and include a headline style known at the school as 'headline-ese.' Students are taught a variety of writing styles and formats such as news, sports and feature writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must learn multiple journalistic formats and the school's specific headline conventions (headline-ese) as part of core journalism training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photojournalism composition and technical skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Photojournalism courses focus on composition, exposure and general camera operation skills. Flash photography is introduced in the basic photography course. Students learn advanced photo-editing, composition and other techniques not taught in basic photojournalism classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progressive training: basic camera and exposure skills in initial courses, with advanced editing and compositional techniques taught in follow-on classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass Communication course progression and occupational awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For military journalists, DINFOS offers the 6-month Mass Communication Fundamentals Course (MCF), two-week Intermediate Public Affairs Specialist Course (IPASC) and four-week Content Management Course. U.S. Army students are awarded the MOS 46S (Mass Communications Specialist), U.S. Air Force students AFSC 3N0X6 (Public Affairs), and U.S. Marine Corps students MOS 4500 (Communication and Multi Media Specialist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course durations and the occupational specialty/AFSC/MOS designations awarded upon successful completion are specified as outcomes of the training pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast training progression and BWAS prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: For military Broadcast journalists, DINFOS offers the Broadcast Communication Specialist Course. Broadcasters begin by attending several weeks of BWAS - Basic Writing and Announcing Skills. If the class requirements are met, students may continue into Radio and Television broadcasting classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progression to radio/TV broadcasting courses is conditional on meeting BWAS class requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television equipment maintenance competency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Basic Television Equipment Maintenance (BTVEM) course includes apprentice level instruction in the repair of all types of studio and transmission equipment. Students also learn how to maintain the Adobe Premiere non-linear digital editing systems. The U.S. Army MOS 25R is awarded upon completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course describes specific technical competencies (repair and maintenance, Premiere systems) and the MOS awarded upon successful completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFRTS engineering standards and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broadcast Radio and Television Systems Maintenance course is an advanced level course where students learn the ins and outs of American Forces Radio and Television Service (AFRTS) engineering standards and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced course focused on AFRTS-specific engineering standards; indicates subject-matter depth required for systems maintenance roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Society of Broadcast Engineers (SBE) certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Both maintenance courses are nationally accredited by the Society of Broadcast Engineers (SBE). Upon completion of either course with an average GPA of at least 85%, students are certified by the SBE as broadcast technologists (CBT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit numeric performance threshold (average GPA >= 85%) required for SBE certification; links course completion to national professional credential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accreditation and ACE credit recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1995, DINFOS is accredited by the Council on Occupational Education. The American Council on Education (ACE) recommends college credit for most DINFOS courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates institutional accreditation and that many courses have been evaluated for college credit recommendation by ACE — relevant for transfer/recognition of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Public Affairs Leadership courses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Affairs Leadership Department offers the Qualification Course (PAQC), the Joint Expeditionary Course (JEPAC), the Joint Intermediate Course (JIPAC), and the Joint Senior Course (JSPAC). Courses are offered to military officers, senior enlisted personnel, Department of Defense civilians, and members of coalition partners preparing for or already in billets of public affairs leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies target audience/eligibility for leadership-track public affairs courses (rank/role and coalition partners).
